annotation.title_clean: Pros and Cons of AI Robot as a Legal Subject
annotation.title_en: Pros and Cons of AI Robot as a Legal Subject
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Prianto, Y.; Sumantri, V.K.; Sasmita, P.Y.
annotation.venue: Advances in Social Science, Education and Humanities Research, vol. 439 (TICASH 2019), Atlantis Press
named_instruments_referenced: PDPC Singapore Discussion Paper on AI and Personal Data
annotation.summary_en: This Indonesian conference paper uses normative legal research to weigh the pros and cons of treating AI robots as legal subjects. It draws on cases such as Sophia's Saudi citizenship and Facebook's chatbots. It argues that AI robots now sit in a legal grey area. Lawmakers, courts and academics should therefore develop rules on how humans relate to autonomous AI robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots with AI are being treated in different ways: as goods, as something like pets, or as legal subjects comparable to humans and corporations.
Giving citizenship to Sophia and residency to Shibuya Mirai caused legal confusion over robots' rights and duties.
Because AI robots can act beyond their owners' control, they currently fall in a regulatory grey area.
Lawmakers should work with AI experts on fair, light-touch rules that support innovation.
The paper reviews the Asilomar AI Principles, including human control and avoiding an AI arms race.
